source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-12), MongoosT-50LH (BE) left-hand grip seen from behind and the left: head face with the red button and five hats/buttons toward the viewer, front of the grip to the left (red trigger and the grey curved lever under the head tip, ribbed side switch on the head front), brake lever at the lower front, knurled grip nut at the bottom
mappingSource: catalog has no input numbers (no official button map survives; product pages https://virpil-controls.eu/vpc-mongoost-50lh-grip.html and https://virpil-controls.eu/vpc-mongoost-50lh-be-grip.html list the control set). Identities taken from the product description and by analogy with the successor's official sheet (MongoosT-50CM2 grip, https://support.virpil.com/en/support/solutions/articles/47001250820-vpc-mongoost-50cm2-grip), whose head has the same layout (mirrored here)
note: mirror image of virpil-mongoost-50-grip (same JoyPro order there). Positions are sure; which catalog part each hat/button is is NOT (the catalog names them only hat.1-3 and button 1-4), so those are hidden candidates (medium map=low) in a JoyPro order: hat.1 stepped square hat, hat.2 concentric hat, hat.3 ribbed face hat; thumb.1/thumb.2 the two round face buttons (upper, lower). The other plain buttons and the grip-side domed control are on the far side (gallery-2) and not on this photo. hat.4 (2-position index switch) = the ribbed switch on the front side of the head, by the product description ("index-side") and the CM2 sheet's side rocker at the same spot. Red trigger under the head = dual-stage trigger (same place as the CM2 trigger 1/2). The grey curved lever under the head tip is likely the folding trigger, but the CM2 sheet leaves the same-looking blade unlabeled, so it stays a candidate.
